notes: BakıKart (metro/bus 0.50 AZN); Bolt taxis are cheap. Take the H1 bus to the airport. For Gobustan and Sheki, join a tour or hire a car.
Winter is windy at 2-8°C; March brings Novruz (spring festival, fire jumping). April-May and September-October are ideal, and Sheki in autumn is golden.
Turkish citizens get 30 days visa-free (with ID card from 2025). 1 manat ≈ 0.6 USD; kutab 2 AZN, piti 8, restaurant meals 20-30, museums 5-15; tip 10%.
The Flame Towers light up after 21:00; Yanar Dag is best in the evening; Heydar Aliyev Center is closed on Mondays.
Piti, kutab, plov (shah plov), dolma, levengi, Sheki halva, pomegranate juice, tea in pear-shaped glasses with jam.
Turkish is understood (Azerbaijani Turkish); Russian is widely spoken. An oil city: look for the pumpjacks at Bibi-Heybat.

stops.name: Icherisheher Eski Şehir
stops.tips: A walled 12th-century city and UNESCO site: narrow lanes, the location where the film Brilliant Hand (Elmas Kol) was shot, and carpet sellers.

stops.name: Maiden Tower
stops.tips: A mysterious 8-storey tower (Zoroastrian, perhaps?). From the top you can see the Caspian Sea and the Flame Towers.

stops.name: Palace of the Shirvanshahs
stops.tips: The 15th-century palace of the Shirvanshahs, with a mausoleum, a divan house and a hammam.

stops.name: Firuze Restoranı Eski Şehir
stops.tips: Azerbaijani cuisine: kutab (thin stuffed flatbread), piti (lamb and chickpea stew) and saj (meat and vegetables cooked on a griddle).

stops.name: Baku Boulevard
stops.tips: A 3.7 km promenade (1909) along the Caspian shore, with a Ferris wheel and gondolas in Little Venice. After 20:00 take the funicular up to Highland Park and watch the Flame Towers light show.

backups.name: Sehirli Tendir
backups.tips: Tandir bread (baked in a clay oven) and kutab, on an Old City street.

backups.name: Museum of Miniature Books
backups.tips: Guinness record-holding miniature books. Free entry; an alternative to the palace.

days.theme: Heydar Aliyev and the Carpet Museum

stops.name: Heydar Aliyev Center
stops.tips: Zaha Hadid's wavy white masterpiece, with a classic car exhibition. Photographing the exterior is free.

stops.name: Azerbaijan Carpet Museum
stops.tips: A building shaped like a rolled carpet, on the Boulevard, with weaving demonstrations.

stops.name: Nargiz Restaurant Bulvar
stops.tips: Azerbaijani food with Caspian views: dolma and kebab.

stops.name: Nizami Street Torgovaya
stops.tips: A pedestrian shopping street lined with 19th-century oil baron buildings.

stops.name: Baku Crystal Hall & Flag Square Walk
stops.tips: The Eurovision 2012 arena. Watch the sunset at the end of the Boulevard.

backups.name: Museum of Modern Art Baku
backups.tips: Azerbaijani modern art; an alternative to the carpet museum.

backups.name: Paul's Bakery Fountains Square
backups.tips: Coffee and pastries on the square.

stops.name: Gobustan Rock Art
stops.tips: 60 km south (tour about 40 AZN, or take a taxi). More than 6,000 rock carvings up to 10,000 years old, a UNESCO site, with a museum.

stops.name: Gobustan Mud Volcanoes
stops.tips: Azerbaijan has half of the world's mud volcanoes: bubbling cones of cold mud, reached by old Lada.

stops.name: Bibi-Heybat Mosque
stops.tips: A mosque on the Caspian shore, destroyed by the Soviets and later rebuilt, set among oil pumpjacks.

stops.name: Qobustan Yolu Balık Lokantası
stops.tips: Caspian fish (kutum) and levengi (stuffed fish or chicken), on the way.

stops.name: Yanar Dag
stops.tips: A gas-fed hillside that has burned continuously for 60 years, tied to Zoroastrian tradition. Striking in the dark of evening, 25 km north.

backups.name: Ateshgah Fire Temple
backups.tips: The Surakhani Zoroastrian-Hindu fire temple, in the same direction as Yanar Dag. Visit instead of it or as an addition.

backups.name: Qala Köy Restoranı
backups.tips: Tandir and saj next to the ethnographic village; an alternative to the roadside restaurant.

stops.name: Ateshgah of Baku
stops.tips: The Surakhani fire temple (17th-century Hindu-Zoroastrian), with a natural gas flame and pilgrim cells.

stops.name: Qala Archaeological Ethnographic Complex
stops.tips: An open-air museum village on the Absheron peninsula, with a fortress, tandir ovens and camels.

stops.name: Mardakan Fortress & Town
stops.tips: A 14th-century fortress and arboretum, plus Yesenin's house.

stops.name: Mardakan Balık Tavernası
stops.tips: Grilled fish in a seaside town.

stops.name: Bilgah Beach
stops.tips: The winter Caspian wind and a walk along the shore.

backups.name: Amburan Beach Club
backups.tips: A beach club with sun loungers, in Bilgah.

backups.name: Gala Köyü Çayhanesi
backups.tips: Tea in pear-shaped glasses with jam, in the village.

stops.name: Sheki Khan's Palace
stops.tips: 4 hours from Baku (early tour or car; staying overnight is ideal). A palace built in 1762 with shebeke stained glass, a UNESCO site, built without nails.

stops.name: Sheki Caravanserai
stops.tips: An 18th-century caravanserai hotel, with a courtyard and vaults.

stops.name: Şeki Piti Öğle Gagarin
stops.tips: Sheki's piti soup served in an earthenware pot (the ritual: first dip bread in the broth, then mash the meat). Try Sheki halva too.

stops.name: Kish Albanian Church
stops.tips: A Caucasian Albanian church (legend dates it to the 1st century), linked to Thor Heyerdahl's theory, in the village.

stops.name: Şeki Halva Atölyesi
stops.tips: Sheki halva to take home, on the way back (Baku 20:00).

backups.name: Gabala Tufandag Cable Car
backups.tips: A Caucasus mountain cable car and Lake Nohur; closer than Sheki (3 hours), so a good alternative.

backups.name: Lahıc Köy Çayhanesi
backups.tips: Tea and kebab in a cobbled coppersmith village; an alternative on the road to Sheki.

stops.name: Taza Bazaar
stops.tips: A local market: pomegranates, saffron, sumac, cheese tasting and dried fruit.

stops.name: Baku Funicular & Martyrs' Lane Daytime
stops.tips: See Martyrs' Lane and the Eternal Flame by day, plus the Turkish Martyrs' Mosque.

stops.name: Sumakh Restaurant
stops.tips: Stylish Azerbaijani cuisine: saj and kutab, in Khagani.

stops.name: Baku Sea Boat Tour
stops.tips: A 1-hour Caspian boat tour from the Boulevard, with the skyline views.

stops.name: Nizami Cinema & Passage Cafes Evening
stops.tips: Seaside Park and the tea houses of Torgovaya, with shisha.

backups.name: Stone Chronicle Museum
backups.tips: A museum of stone inscriptions, on the Boulevard.

backups.name: Çay Bağı 145 Eski Şehir
backups.tips: Tea and jam in the Old City, in the Azerbaijani tea tradition.

days.theme: Boulevard morning and a gentle farewell

stops.name: Little Venice Boulevard Morning Walk
stops.tips: Canals with gondolas and morning calm.

stops.name: Mugham Center
stops.tips: A building shaped like a tar (a stringed instrument), on the Boulevard. See it from outside.

stops.name: Qaynana Restoranı Kahvaltı
stops.tips: Azerbaijani breakfast: clotted cream, honey, tandir bread and kuymak (a cornmeal and cheese dish), next to Fountains Square.

stops.name: Baku Airport Bus H1
stops.tips: The H1 bus runs from 28 May and takes 40 minutes (BakıKart). Time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Ali and Nino Kitapçı Kafe
backups.tips: Breakfast in a bookshop cafe, in the city of the novel.

backups.name: Government House
backups.tips: A giant Stalin-era building on Azadliq Square. See it from outside.
